claims.text: The starting material is a solid solution containing at least five elements, each at no less than 5 atomic percent.
The starting material is distinct from Nb-Ta and titanium-rich superconducting alloy systems.
Elemental composition can be varied while retaining at least five elements at concentrations of at least 5 atomic percent each.
Changing elemental composition changes the electron density of states at the Fermi level.
The electron density of states at the Fermi level governs superconducting behavior in the alloy.
Changes in the electron density of states at the Fermi level influence superconducting transition temperature.
Systematic changes in elemental composition will produce changes in superconducting transition temperature relative to the starting composition.
The superconducting transition temperature of the starting composition serves as the experimental baseline.
The proposed comparison applies under cryogenic conditions.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to solid solutions containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each.
Failure to observe a significant transition-temperature change across the composition variations would falsify the hypothesis.
